clue.text: First principle: weakest one must receive coin

indicators.note: the weakling has to take the coin into its middle, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the runt is the weakest one of a litter
a dime is a ten-cent coin

explanation.surface: A maxim: the feeblest person ought to be handed money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weakest one' is the runt of a litter; the dime is an American ten-cent coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is a basic element or elementary principle of a subject, the first thing learnt.

clue.text: Jump over to top of knapsack and rearrange contents

indicators.note: the jump is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a caper is a leap

indicators.note: the first letter of knapsack is its top in a down clue

explanation.surface: Hop over to the rucksack and sort out what is in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses CAPER to REPAC; 'top of' gives K.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to pack again, putting the contents back in a new way.

clue.text: Routine ——— it could get boring

explanation.definitionFit: A drill is both a rehearsed routine and a tool for making holes.

clue.text: Horse-and-buggy kept inside — that's sick

indicators.note: the carriage is held within the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a small horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: Something about an old horse-drawn carriage is gruesome.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphens are surface glue: 'Horse' and 'buggy' must be taken separately, 'buggy' being a small carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome, and sick humour is macabre humour.

clue.text: Rebuilt railway termini out of line? No, never!

indicators.note: the letters are put together again in a new order
the ends of the railway are its terminal letters

explanation.surface: A railway's end stations, rebuilt off-line? Certainly not!
explanation.walkthrough: 'termini' gives RY from railway; 'Rebuilt' rearranges RY, OUTOFLINE and NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic refusal, meaning certainly not or never.

clue.text: The significance of an introduction

definitions.meaning: ... as a noun means importance or meaning
something brought in from abroad, introduced into the country

explanation.definitionFit: Import means both meaning or weight and a thing brought in from overseas.

clue.text: Parent's pet dog

parts.note: Ma is a mother, a parent, and the 's gives Ma's
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff

explanation.surface: Mum's beloved dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like an adjective, but means a huff or sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: In accord, if men do no wrong

indicators.note: the letters are put wrong, into a new order

explanation.surface: Agreement holds if men do no wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges IFMENDONO.
explanation.definitionFit: Of one mind means in full agreement.

clue.text: Series of matches —— articles by women…

parts.note: the is the definite article
a is the indefinite article
shes are females, women

explanation.surface: Female writers produce pieces about a sporting series.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ashes is a series of Test cricket matches played for an urn.

clue.text: New charge about to be given weight by university

indicators.note: the charge goes round the new, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a price is what is charged
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A fresh fee is about to be loaded onto students by their university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the containment signal here, not a word for C or RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey.

clue.text: …almost want match transformed by inferior batsman

parts.note: nigh means nearly, almost

indicators.note: the two words are changed into a new arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Having nearly lost a game, the side is turned around by a lowly batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges WANT and MATCH into WATCHMAN. A nightwatchman is a lower-order cricketer sent in late in a day's play to shield a better batsman. The ellipsis links the clue to 8-down's cricket series.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the nightwatchman is a weaker lower-order player promoted to bat out the last overs of a day.

clue.text: Scratch marks

definitions.meaning: to scratch a surface is to scrape a line into it
a test's marks are its tally of points

explanation.definitionFit: Score means both to scratch a line into something and a total of points gained.

clue.text: Sycorax's son, a party member, put in prison

indicators.note: the a and party member are placed inside the prison

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Lib is short for a Liberal, a member of that party

explanation.surface: A political figure gets locked up in jail, and he is somebody's son.
explanation.walkthrough: Sycorax is the witch in Shakespeare's The Tempest; 'Lib' is short for a Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Tempest, the monster Caliban is the son of the witch Sycorax.

clue.text: Protection for the legs from reptiles, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the reptiles are said out loud and the entry is a word that sounds the same

parts.note: gators is short for alligators, which are reptiles

explanation.surface: Something guards your shins against crocodilian attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaiters are coverings of cloth or leather worn over the shin and ankle to protect them.

clue.text: Volunteers may behave inappropriately

definitions.meaning: a soldier volunteering steps forward from the ranks
to misbehave or break with accepted conduct

explanation.surface: Those who offer to help may end up acting badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally stepping forward from a rank, and idiomatically misbehaving.

clue.text: Tradesman standing before Queen

indicators.note: the standing comes before the queen

parts.note: station means standing or rank in society
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is waiting ahead of the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationer is a tradesman who sells paper, pens and writing materials.

clue.text: I must avoid ferocious criminal, need I say

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent, so the letters are reordered
the I is kept out, deleted from the letters

explanation.surface: I'd better steer clear of a violent lawbreaker, obviously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must avoid' removes I from FEROCIOUS; 'criminal' rearranges the remaining FEROCOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course means naturally, as is obvious without being said.

clue.text: Thunderstruck and shaken, gabbled faster

indicators.note: the two words are shaken up so their letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stunned and rattled spoke even more quickly and incoherently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaken' rearranges GABBLED and FASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabbergasted means astonished, as overwhelmed as if struck by thunder.

clue.text: Most daring baronet hosts wild parties

indicators.note: the baronet holds the parties within him

parts.note: raves are wild parties

explanation.surface: The boldest titled gentleman throws riotous parties.
explanation.walkthrough: A baronet is a British hereditary title below a baron, abbreviated Bt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravest is the superlative of brave, meaning most daring.

clue.text: Capital in till now coin's been removed

parts.note: till and to both mean until, as in nine till five

indicators.note: the coin has been taken away, with 's standing for has

parts.note: pronto means at once, now
p is a penny, a British coin

explanation.surface: Money in the cash register has just been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is the provincial capital of Ontario, not Canada's. 'till' looks like a cash register but means until; ''s been removed' takes P from PRONTO, leaving RONTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Toronto is the capital city of the Canadian province of Ontario.

clue.text: Contractor haggles, seemingly for big reduction

indicators.note: a big reduction cuts the two words heavily at both ends, leaving a run from inside them

explanation.surface: A tenant bargains hard, apparently in pursuit of a large discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for big reduction' trims HAGGLES SEEMINGLY down to the run across the comma. 'Contractor' looks like a builder, but is a party to a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A lessee contracts to rent property under a lease, so is a party to a contract.

clue.text: Eastern art displayed by ring road round capital

indicators.note: the ring and road go round the capital, surrounding it

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
the M1 is a British motorway, written MI
Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: An oriental craft is on show, with a ring road circling a city.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Yorkshire; Riga is the Latvian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami, the folding of paper into shapes, is a traditional Japanese art.

clue.text: With stick stuck in the middle of fruit, eat…

indicators.note: the stick is pushed into the fruit's middle

parts.note: the core is the centre of an apple or pear
a rod is a stick

explanation.surface: A skewer pushed into a piece of fruit, then a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the middle of' looks like a containment signal, but 'the middle of fruit' is CORE; the ellipsis runs on into 23-across.
explanation.definitionFit: To corrode is to eat away at metal, as rust does.

clue.text: Look up and study meaning of "of yore"

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
a den is a study

explanation.surface: Consult the dictionary for an archaic phrase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is a reversal signal in a down clue; 'Lo' is an old word for look.
explanation.definitionFit: Olden means of former times, long ago, as of yore does.

clue.text: … a line of peeled fruits

indicators.note: the fruits lose their outer layer, here their first and last letters

parts.note: oranges are fruits

explanation.surface: A row of fruits stripped of their skins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peeled' strips O and S from ORANGES. The ellipses join this clue to 21-across as one sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or row, as of mountains.

clue.text: Females furious as chaps from Brussels have day in Rome

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the European Union, EU
chaps are men
the Ides was a day in the ancient Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month

explanation.surface: Women are angry that European officials are spending a day in Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The page carries the clue's end over into the next column, which the held text lost.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eumenides are a euphemistic name for the Furies, avenging goddesses of Greek myth.

clue.text: In time, informer will make mistakes

indicators.note: the informer goes inside the time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is one who tells on others

explanation.surface: Eventually a snitch will slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'informer' is a rat, the usual crossword snitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are errors, especially those listed for correction in a book.

clue.text: Make public weight girl had put on

indicators.note: the weight is placed after the girl

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: Reveal that a young woman has gained some pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to declare publicly.
